findings.claim: The Eduqas Shakespeare question prints an extract and asks two questions: Part (i) on the extract (20 marks) and Part (ii) on the play as a whole (20 marks). Both assess AO1 (understanding), AO2 (language, form and structure) and AO4 (context).
findings.truth: The spec states no per-part mark split for the Shakespeare section, only that it is 40 marks tested through one extract-based question and one essay question on the text as a whole. AO4 is accurate vocabulary, sentence structure, spelling and punctuation, NOT context. AO3 (context) is not assessed on this section at all, so the follow-up advice to 'practise embedding context within analysis' sends students after marks that do not exist.
findings.evidence: spec 2.1: 'Section A (20%) Shakespeare (40 marks) ... one extract-based question and one essay question on the text as a whole ... Section A assesses AO1, AO2 and AO4.'; spec AO4 definition: 'Use a range of vocabulary and sentence structures for clarity, purpose and effect, with accurate spelling and punctuation.' Grep of the spec for 15/25 finds only AO percentage weightings, no question split.

findings.claim: For context (AO4), always embed it within your analysis. Do not write a separate paragraph about 'Shakespeare's time.' Instead: [worked example of a context sentence]
findings.truth: The whole tip teaches a skill that earns nothing. Context (AO3) is not assessed on the Shakespeare section, and AO4 is written accuracy. The tip should tell students that context is not assessed here and that the marks are AO1, AO2 and AO4.
findings.evidence: spec 2.1: 'Section A assesses AO1, AO2 and AO4.' (AO3 appears only for Section B poetry and Component 2.)

findings.claim: Collapsible heading 'Eduqas C720U: Component 1, Section A'; plus 'For the Eduqas exam, this duality is essential', 'For the Eduqas exam, the strongest responses...', 'Top-band Eduqas responses...', and flashcard 'What top-band approach do Eduqas reward on Henry V?'
findings.truth: Banned strings: 'Component 1' and the spec code both fail the house validator, and the Eduqas/WJEC house rule forbids naming the board in lesson prose. Neutral phrasing required throughout.
findings.evidence: CHECK_PROMPT banned-string list; house rule for Eduqas/WJEC neutral phrasing.

findings.claim: the Tudor monarchs traced their lineage back to Henry V's Welsh connections, so celebrating Henry flattered Elizabeth I
findings.truth: The Tudors did not descend from Henry V. Henry V's only child was Henry VI. Owen Tudor, a Welshman, married Henry V's WIDOW, Catherine of Valois; their son Edmund Tudor fathered Henry VII. The link to Henry V is by that second marriage, not by descent. Lesson 6 states the relationship correctly ('the Tudors were of Welsh origin'), so Lesson 1 also contradicts the unit.
findings.evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Owen_Tudor - Owen Tudor married 'Catherine of Valois (1401-1437), widow of King Henry V of England'; their son Edmund Tudor was the father of Henry VII.

findings.claim: [10].a 'The Tudors traced lineage to Henry V's Welsh connections - celebrating him flattered Elizabeth.'
findings.truth: Same descent error as F4, in a memorisation card. Corrected to the marriage of Owen Tudor to Henry V's widow.
findings.evidence: As F4.

findings.claim: data-def: 'Shakespeare wrote ten history plays covering the reigns of English kings from Richard II to Richard III.'
findings.truth: Internally inconsistent. Richard II to Richard III is the two tetralogies - eight plays. The count of ten only works if King John and Henry VIII are included, and both fall outside that range.
findings.evidence: Shakespeare's history plays: King John, Richard II, 1-2 Henry IV, Henry V, 1-3 Henry VI, Richard III, Henry VIII.

findings.claim: He insists Canterbury take "heed how you awake our sleeping sword of war"
findings.truth: The quotation marks open one word too early and splice across a cut. The text reads 'Therefore take heed how you impawn our person, / How you awake our sleeping sword of war.' Only 'how you awake our sleeping sword of war' is verbatim.
findings.evidence: Gutenberg #1521 lines 378-379 (Act 1 Scene 2, Henry to Canterbury).

findings.claim: invokes English identity ("the noblest English")
findings.truth: The text reads 'On, on, you noblest English'. The same paragraph quotes it correctly a sentence later, so this is a slip, not a variant reading.
findings.evidence: Gutenberg #1521 line 1637 (Act 3 Scene 1).

findings.claim: This order [to kill the prisoners], given in response to a French attack on the English baggage train, is historically documented, but Shakespeare does not soften it.
findings.truth: In the play the causation runs the other way round. Henry gives the order at 4.6 immediately after 'The French have reinforc'd their scatter'd men'. The killing of the boys with the luggage is not staged or reported until 4.7, where Gower then claims it as the King's reason. Presenting Gower's after-the-fact justification as the trigger removes the crux students are meant to notice.
findings.evidence: Gutenberg #1521 lines 3757-3758 (Act 4 Scene 6, begins line 3705) vs lines 3768 and 3776 (Act 4 Scene 7, begins line 3763).

findings.claim: [3].q 'Henry orders his soldiers to "kill his _____" after the French attack the English baggage train.'
findings.truth: Same reversed sequence as F9 built into a knowledge check. The keyed answer ('prisoners', index 1) stays correct; only the framing is wrong.
findings.evidence: As F9.

findings.claim: Act 4 opens with the Chorus describing the English camp on the eve of battle: exhausted, sick, outnumbered five to one.
findings.truth: The Act 4 Chorus gives no odds. 'There's five to one; besides, they all are fresh' is Westmorland at 4.3, in the scene before the St Crispin's Day speech.
findings.evidence: Gutenberg #1521 line 3328 (Act 4 Scene 3) vs the Act 4 Chorus at lines 2679-2739.

findings.claim: [3].a is the single word "'Ceremony.'" against the question 'Which single empty thing does Henry say a king has?'
findings.truth: House rule: a one-word flashcard answer is only allowed when the question opens What is / Who was / When / Name. Expanded to a full answer that keeps the sense of 'what have kings that privates have not too, / Save ceremony'.
findings.evidence: CHECK_PROMPT validator limits; Gutenberg #1521 line 3113 (Act 4 Scene 1).

findings.claim: The St Crispin's Day speech is the most likely extract for the Eduqas exam.
findings.truth: Names the board, against the house rule, and over-claims certainty about the extract choice.
findings.evidence: House rule for Eduqas/WJEC neutral phrasing.

findings.claim: The French King blesses the marriage with hopes that "English may as French, French Englishmen, / Receive each other."
findings.truth: Wrong speaker. Those lines are Queen Isabel's blessing at the end of 5.2. The French King's speeches in the scene are about terms and about his daughter, not this blessing.
findings.evidence: Gutenberg #1521 lines 4919-4929: 'QUEEN ISABEL. God, the best maker of all marriages ... That English may as French, French Englishmen, / Receive each other.'

findings.claim: focus on ... Katherine's lack of genuine choice (AO4: women's agency in Elizabethan/medieval society)
findings.truth: AO4 is written accuracy, not context, and context (AO3) is not assessed on the Shakespeare section. The point about Katherine is still worth making, but as AO1/AO2 - who speaks, how much and in which language.
findings.evidence: spec 2.1 'Section A assesses AO1, AO2 and AO4'; spec AO4 definition.

findings.claim: Henry V is the only Shakespeare play to use a Chorus that speaks before every act (repeated in the glossary as 'Unique to Henry V among Shakespeare's plays' and in a flashcard question).
findings.truth: Not the only one. In Pericles, Gower speaks a prologue before every act and delivers the epilogue. Henry V is the only one of the history plays to do it, which is the claim worth keeping.
findings.evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pericles,_Prince_of_Tyre - 'John Gower introduces each act with a prologue.'

findings.claim: 'Always embed context within analysis. Check your exam board's specimen paper for the exact wording, timings and mark weightings.'; 'practise weaving context into your analysis'; 'Many papers are closed-book'; 'This dual reading is what earns Band 5.'; description and four data items naming Eduqas and the spec code; flashcard answer 'Printed extract, Part (i) extract analysis (20m), Part (ii) whole-text with context (20m).'
findings.truth: Context is not assessed on the Shakespeare section, so the two 'embed context' instructions send students after marks that do not exist and the flashcard structure card is wrong twice over (it also asserts a 20+20 split the spec does not state, and is a bare comma list). This section IS closed-book, definitely, not 'many papers'. The board name and spec code breach the house rule and the banned-string list, and 'Band 5' mimics board band naming - the house ladder says top band. Real figures the spec does support: 40 marks for the section, 2 hours for the whole component across two equally weighted sections, so about an hour here.
findings.evidence: spec 2.1: 40 marks, 'Learners are not permitted to take copies of the set texts into the examination', 'Written examination: 2 hours', Sections A and B both 20%.

findings.claim: All 48 practice questions across the eight lessons are labelled '[20]' with type '20 marks - Extract Analysis' or '20 marks - Wider Text Response', and each ladder runs 1-20 in five equal bands.
findings.truth: The spec gives the section as 40 marks through one extract question and one essay question, and states no split between them. 20 + 20 is therefore an assumption, not a fact - and the real papers may well use an uneven split. The drills are at least internally coherent (ladder tops match the label, and two 20s sum to the correct 40), so they are not malformed. My recommendation: leave the 48 drill labels as they are, and fix only the prose and flashcard sentences that state the split as exam fact (done in F1 and F17). If someone can check a real past paper and the split is uneven, all 48 labels, types and ladders need a single scripted rescale to the true marks, in five equal house bands. ORCHESTRATOR: left as 20-mark items; the spec states no per-part split, so no rescale without a sample-paper check (corpus note).
findings.evidence: spec 2.1; grep of the spec for '15' and '25' returns only AO weighting percentages, no per-question marks.

findings.claim: Every ladder's bottom band is named 'Lower band (1-4)'.
findings.truth: The house ladder names the bottom band 'Low band'. Not a banned string and not a factual error, so not worth 48 edits on its own - but if F18 triggers a scripted rescale, rename it in the same pass.
findings.evidence: CHECK_PROMPT house ladder: Top / Upper-mid / Mid / Lower-mid / Low / Basic.

findings.claim: Katherine's line is quoted four times as 'Dat is as it shall please de roi mon pere'.
findings.truth: The curated Gutenberg text reads 'le roi mon pere'. 'De roi' follows the Folio, which renders Katherine's accent, and is the reading in several modern editions. A defensible editorial variant, not an error - recorded so nobody 'corrects' it later.
findings.evidence: Gutenberg #1521 line 4748 (Act 5 Scene 2).

findings.claim: Lesson title 'Key Themes & Exam Technique' is fine, but the lesson description named the board.
findings.truth: No title change needed anywhere in the unit. All eight titles match their content. Recorded only to confirm the titles were checked.
findings.evidence: Brief lesson list vs raw lesson content.

summary: Every quotation in the unit checks out against the Gutenberg text for wording, act and scene, with two slips in quotation-mark placement (L2, L3) and one line given to the wrong speaker (L5: Queen Isabel's blessing attributed to the French King). The serious damage is in the exam material: three lessons teach that AO4 is context and tell students to embed context in the Shakespeare answer, when context is not assessed on that section at all, and the unit states a 20+20 mark split the spec does not give. Also fixed: the Tudor descent from Henry V (they descend from his widow's second marriage), the reversed cause of the order to kill the prisoners, the 'only Shakespeare play with a Chorus' claim (Pericles), and every banned string - 'Component 1', the spec code, the board name and 'Band 5'.
